title: Family-led intensive care diaries and post-intensive care syndrome: a narrative review for a unit guideline
subtitle: Narrative review for a unit guideline and teaching day, ICU follow-up clinic
statement: Families of patients ventilated for more than 72 hours on a 24-bed intensive care unit have been offered a diary since March 2025, and about half accept. The follow-up clinic sees patients with nightmares, flashbacks and memory gaps, and relatives with persistent distress. Clinicians disagree about whether diaries written mainly by families help. The unit needs a narrative review that states what the evidence shows about effects in patients and relatives, harms of reading, and how programmes are run, with an honest account of its certainty.
whoAffected: Adult intensive care survivors ventilated for more than 72 hours, their relatives (including bereaved relatives), the nurses who support diary writing and the follow-up clinic team.
whatHurts: Post-traumatic stress, anxiety and depression after intensive care affect both patients and relatives; memory gaps and intrusive memories are common at the 3-month clinic, and a programme without clear guidance may cause distress or reach only some families.
currentPractice: Paper diaries offered to families of patients ventilated for more than 72 hours, a one-page writing guide and twice-weekly nurse contact; the diary is handed over at discharge without a set reading visit.
whyNow: The education committee wants a unit guideline and a teaching day in spring 2027, and staff views on diaries are divided.
constraints: No research funding; 40 hours of protected time between October 2026 and February 2027; searches only through the hospital library service; the unit guideline and teaching day are due in March 2027.
patientCenteredGoal: Patients and relatives who are offered a diary receive one that is written, read and followed up in the way most likely to help and least likely to harm.
summary: Problem framed as a narrative review of family-led diaries and post-intensive care syndrome to inform a unit guideline.
